item.title: C*-algebras of Essentially Tracially Rank One
item.description: arXiv:2610.14711v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the notion of essential tracial rank at most one for simple $C^*$-algebras. We show that separable simple $C^*$-algebras with essential tracial rank at most one have several regularity properties, including stable rank one, strict comparison, and tracial approximate divisibility. A finite amenable simple $C^*$-algebras with this property is $\mathcal Z$-stable. We also prove the converse. Thus this property gives a new characterization of separable simple finite amenable $\mathcal Z$-stable $C^*$-algebras and shows that these algebras admit a one-dimensional tracial approximation. In the unital real-rank-zero case, this approximation can be strengthened to show that the algebra has tracial rank zero. This completes a long-standing project. As a byproduct, we prove that every tracial state on a unital separable simple finite amenable $C^*$-algebra is quasidiagonal and that the algebra itself is quasidiagonal. Consequently, every separable simple finite amenable $C^*$-algebra of finite nuclear dimension has finite decomposition rank. None of these results requires the UCT.
item.dc:creator: Huaxin Lin

item.title: Zero-divisor graphs and zero-divisor real rank of $C^*$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.15160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study two invariants of $C^*$-algebras built from positive zero divisors. First, we associate with a $C^*$-algebra $A$ the graph $\Gamma_+(A)$ whose vertices are the nonzero positive zero divisors of $A$, two vertices being adjacent when they are orthogonal. We show that $\Gamma_+$ of the Calkin algebra is connected of diameter $3$, that $\Gamma_+(B(H))$ is connected of diameter $4$ (for $\dim H\ge3$), that $\Gamma_+(A)$ is connected of diameter at most $4$ for every von Neumann factor $A\neq\mathbb C,M_2(\mathbb C)$, and of diameter at most $3$ if $A$ is not of type~I, whereas $\Gamma_+(M_2(\mathbb C))$ is disconnected. Second, we study the zero-divisor real rank $ZDRR(A)$, obtained by replacing invertibility in the definition of real rank with the weaker condition of being a non-zero-divisor, so that $ZDRR(A)\le RR(A)$. For commutative algebras $C(X)$ we prove $ZDRR(C(X))=RR(C(X))=\dim X$ when $X$ is a compact almost-$P$-space, while $ZDRR(C(X))=0$ for separable $X$. Using Levy's connected, totally ordered almost-$P$-space we construct unital commutative $C^*$-algebras $A_n$ with $ZDRR(A_n)=n$ for every $n\in\mathbb N_0$. On the other hand $ZDRR(C(X\times[0,1]))=0$ for every compact Hausdorff space $X$, so $ZDRR$ and $RR$ can differ arbitrarily.
item.dc:creator: Ali Taghavi

item.title: On the set of orthogonal positive sums in a $C^*$-algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.15167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a $C^*$-algebra $A$ let $\mathcal I(A)$ be the set of all elements $a+b$ with $a,b\in A_+$, $ab=0$ and $\|a\|=\|b\|=1$. We study the algebraic, metric and topological properties of $\mathcal I(A)$. We describe $\mathcal I(A\oplus B)$ and show that $\mathcal I(A/J)\subseteq\pi(\mathcal I(A))$ for the quotient map $\pi:A\to A/J$. For finite-dimensional $A$ we prove $\mathcal I(A)=\operatorname{Sph}^+_A(E(A))$, where $E(A)$ is the set of minimal projections of $A$ and $\operatorname{Sph}^+_A(E)$ is the set of positive norm-one elements at distance one from every element of $E$; we also show that the analogous statement with the minimal projections of the bidual fails in general. When $\mathcal I(A)\neq\varnothing$ the distance from $1$ to $\mathcal I(A)$ is $0$ or $1$, according to whether $A$ has a nontrivial projection. Moreover, $\mathcal I(A)$ is norm compact if and only if $A$ is finite-dimensional, closedness of $\mathcal I(A)$ passes to hereditary subalgebras, $\mathcal I(A)$ is norm closed for every von Neumann algebra, and the extreme points of $\mathcal I(A)$ are exactly its projections. For a compact, locally path connected space $X$ the set $\mathcal I(C(X))$ is closed, whereas $\mathcal I(\ell_c(A))$ fails to be closed when $A$ is unital without nontrivial projections.
item.dc:creator: Ali Taghavi

item.title: Fuglede--Kadison Determinants of Shifted Matrix Semicircles
item.description: arXiv:2610.15180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a variational formula for the Fuglede-Kadison determinant of a self-adjoint matrix semicircle $S_a = a \otimes 1 + \sum_j A_j \otimes s_j$ with deterministic mean $a$. For every real $z$, $\log \Delta(S_a - z) = -1/2 + \inf_b F_z(b)$, where the infimum is over positive definite matrices $b$ such that the map $X \mapsto bXb - \sum_j A_j X A_j$ is positive semidefinite, and $F_z$ is an explicit geodesically convex function. Both sides equal $-\infty$ exactly when $z$ is an atom of the spectral measure. The formula was proposed, without proof, in a recent post of Speicher. In the centered case $a=0$ it gives a new proof of the Mai-Speicher capacity formula, and by hermitization it yields a finite-dimensional variational formula for the logarithmic potential of the Brown measure of an arbitrary matrix-valued semicircular element. The proof identifies the determinant with the value of the Dyson action at its critical point and rewrites this critical-point problem as a saddle problem in three matrix variables. For a spectral parameter $z + i\varepsilon$ in the upper half-plane, eliminating two of the variables gives a geodesically convex minimization whose global minimizer is the positive factor $b_\varepsilon$ in a symmetric unitary factorization of the matrix Cauchy transform. The formula on the real axis follows by letting $\varepsilon \to 0$ in the optimal values, with no compactness assumption on the minimizers. At points where the boundary value of the Cauchy transform is nondegenerate, the scales $b_\varepsilon$ converge and the infimum is attained at their limit; this minimizer lies on the boundary of the feasible set when $z$ is in the support of the spectral measure and in its interior when $z$ is in the resolvent set.
item.dc:creator: Vladislav Kargin

item.title: Quadratic polynomials preserving free infinite divisibility
item.description: arXiv:2610.15320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize non-commutative polynomials of degree 2 which preserve free infinite divisibility as self-adjoint Lie polynomials of degree 2. This extends previous results which characterized homogeneous quadratic forms only. The proof is based on an involution of colored noncrossing partitions cancelling many terms; positive definiteness of the remaining terms is established by an explicit operator model on Fock space. Examples show that higher order Lie polynomials do not preserve free infinite divisibility.
item.dc:creator: Wiktor Ejsmont, Franz Lehner, Mihai Popa, Kamil Szpojankowski

item.title: Spectral geometry of saturated Fell bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.15395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal B=(B_g)_{g\in G}$ be a saturated Fell bundle over a countable discrete group, equipped with a spectral triple. We give explicit sufficient conditions for lifting this triple to the reduced cross-sectional C\Star-algebra $C_r^*(\mathcal B)$. Using finite projective realizations of the homogeneous Morita equivalence $B_e$-bimodules, we transport the base Dirac operator to the individual fibres and assemble the resulting operators into a fibrewise Dirac operator. We introduce a spectral-regularity condition ensuring bounded commutators and give a sufficient criterion in terms of uniform derivative bounds on smooth factor-system data. Combining the fibrewise operator with a length operator associated with a proper translation-bounded matrix-valued length function yields the lifted spectral triple. When $B_e$ is separable, the lifted triple, with a suitable grading, represents the Kasparov product of the vertical class with the class of the unit-fibre triple. We also establish a summability criterion and sufficient conditions for stability under central cocycle twisting. A range of examples illustrates the scope of the construction, including twisted crossed products, free compact Abelian actions, and Fell bundles with nonfree homogeneous fibres.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Wagner

item.title: Quantum integrals II: Dominated and almost uniform convergence
item.description: arXiv:2610.16499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: One main aim of our paper is to formulate noncommutative versions of the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem in the setting of quantum integration theory on von Neumann algebras. Our starting point is a reformulation of classical dominated convergence in terms of weak* convergence. Using our recent sequential-continuity theorem, we obtain dominated convergence formulations for sequentially normal states and, under domination by a fixed bounded integrable majorant, for sequentially normal weights. Integrable, possibly unbounded, majorants are treated first in the tracial setting, then for arbitrary von Neumann algebras using Haagerup's L1 space, and finally using normal semifinite weights and their GNS representations. For any faithful normal semifinite weight $\phi$, weak* convergence of norm-bounded sequences is characterized by `integrating against' bounded positive integrable majorants. We also study noncommutative almost uniform and local almost uniform convergence. In particular, for norm-bounded sequences, local $\phi$-bilaterally almost uniform convergence implies weak* convergence and L1 convergence to 0 of $h^{1/2}(x_n-x)h^{1/2}$ for every positive Haagerup L1 density h, without assuming sigma-finiteness. We also prove a dominated convergence theorem in the predual: fixed positive order domination and Petz's almost uniform convergence imply convergence in the predual norm. We establish implications and equivalences among these convergence notions, connecting dominated convergence with tracial and nontracial integration.
item.dc:creator: David P. Blecher

item.title: Pointwise Ergodic Theorems Along Reiter Sequences on Locally Compact Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.16580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a locally compact, second countable group admitting a Reiter sequence, and suppose that $G$ acts on a von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$ equipped with a semifinite trace $\tau$ via trace-preserving automorphisms. In this paper, we prove a maximal inequality for ergodic averages along such Reiter sequences. Our approach relies on approximating the Reiter sequence by a linear combination of characteristic functions of F{\o}lner sequences using the layer-cake representation. Furthermore, we establish the bilateral almost uniform convergence of these ergodic averages. As an application, we deduce a non-commutative Wiener-Wintner type theorem along Reiter sequences.
item.dc:creator: Panchugopal Bikram, Sudipta Kundu, Hariharan G, Diptesh Saha

item.title: Endpoint Schatten class properties of commutators on quantum tori
item.description: arXiv:2610.16747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study endpoint Schatten class properties of commutators $[I_\theta^\epsilon,M_x]$ on quantum tori of dimension $d\geq2$, where $I_\theta^\epsilon$ is the Riesz potential of order $\epsilon$ and $M_x$ denotes the left multiplication operator by an operator $x$ on quantum tori $\mathbb T_\theta^d$. For $-\frac{d}{2}<\epsilon<1$, $\epsilon\neq0$, and $x\in L_1(\mathbb T_\theta^d)$, we prove that $[I_\theta^\epsilon,M_x]\in \mathcal L_{\frac{d}{1-\epsilon},\infty}$ if and only if $x\in\dot W_{\frac{d}{1-\epsilon}}^1(\mathbb T_\theta^d)$. We also determine the singular value asymptotics of this commutator for $x\in\dot W_{\frac{d}{1-\epsilon}}^1(\mathbb T_\theta^d)$. The necessary Sobolev condition holds throughout $1-d<\epsilon<1$, $\epsilon\neq0$. For $\epsilon\leq-\frac{d}{2}$, we characterise Hilbert--Schmidt membership, with a logarithmically weighted Fourier condition at $\epsilon=-\frac{d}{2}$. In order to get the singular value asymptotics of commutators, we prove singular value asymptotics for pseudodifferential operators of arbitrary negative order on quantum tori using $C^*$-algebraic principal symbols. This asymptotic result confirms Conjecture~7.1 of McDonald and Ponge (\emph{Adv. Math.} 412 (2023), 108815).
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Zhang

item.title: On the generators of separable unital C*-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.17411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the recent single-generation theorem for von Neumann $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors with separable predual, we prove the following results on the generators of a separable unital C*-algebra. Let $A$ be a separable unital C*-algebra, and suppose that $\partial \mathrm{T}(A)$ is nonempty, compact, and zero-dimensional. Then (1) If $A$ has strict comparison of positive elements by tracial states, then $A$ can be generated by two ordinary elements. (2) If $A$ has real rank zero and $A$ has strict comparison of projections by tracial states, then $A$ is singly generated. In this case, its single generators form a norm-dense $G_\delta$ subset of $A$. (3) If $A$ has strict comparison of positive elements by tracial states and there is a unitary $u\in A$ such that for every $\tau\in \partial \mathrm{T}(A)$, (a): the spectral distribution of $u$ with respect to $\tau$ is atomless and has full support on $\mathbb T$, and (b): for every $a\in A$, $$\lim_{t \to 0}\sup_{p\in D_\tau, 0<\tau(p)\leq t} \| p\bigl(\pi_\tau(a)-\mathbb E_{D_\tau}(\pi_\tau(a))\bigr)p\|=0, $$ where $M_\tau=\pi_\tau(A)''$, $D_\tau=\pi_\tau(u)''$, $\mathbb E_{D_\tau}: M_\tau \to D_\tau$ is the trace-preserving conditional expectation, and $\pi_\tau$ is the GNS representation associated to $\tau$, then $A$ is singly generated. In particular, Conclusion (3) above implies that the reduced group C*-algebra $\mathrm{C}_r^*(\mathbb F_n)$ is singly generated for every $n\in\{2,3,\ldots,\infty\}$.
item.dc:creator: George A. Elliott, Chun Guang Li, Zhuang Niu

item.title: Model theory of quasitracial $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras and the absoluteness of monotone completeness
item.description: arXiv:2610.17435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine various applications of logic to $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras, particularly the monotone completeness conjecture. We develop a model theory for $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras equipped with a faithful normalized quasitrace. Using this language, we provide a separable coding which allows us to reduce the finite case of the monotone completeness conjecture to monotone sequential completeness of $\mathrm{II}_1$ $\mathrm{AW}^*$-factors. Combining an explicit recursive axiomatization with the completeness theorem for continuous logic, we show that this case of the conjecture, and Kaplansky's problem whether every $\mathrm{AW}^*$-factor of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ is a von Neumann algebra, are each equivalent in ZFC to a $\Pi^0_2$ sentence of arithmetic, so that their answers are the same in every $\omega$-model of ZFC. We also consider real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras. Here the Baer-$*$-ring notion of an abelian projection must be distinguished from commutativity; following the real-operator-algebra terminology we call the former semi-abelian. Handelman's matrix theorem implies that a real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebra with no nonzero central semi-abelian projection has $\mathrm{AW}^*$ complexification. We answer a number of other open problems in real $\mathrm{AW}^*$-algebras.
item.dc:creator: Jananan Arulseelan

item.title: Aperiodic automorphisms of the Razak--Jacelon algebra
item.description: arXiv:2610.17543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We completely classify aperiodic automorphisms of the Razak--Jacelon algebra $\mathcal{W}$ up to outer conjugacy. As a technical ingredient, based on the works of Connes, Herman--Ocneanu, Kishimoto, and Sato, we introduce a notion of weak stability for automorphisms of simple separable monotracial C$^*$-algebras. We also consider automorphisms of UHF algebras of infinite type and the Jiang--Su algebra.
item.dc:creator: Norio Nawata

item.title: The $2$-co-lacunary subsequence principle for arbitrary noncommutative $L_1$-spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.18008v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every von Neumann algebra \(\M\), we prove that each bounded sequence in the Haagerup space \(L_1(\M)=\M_*\) admits either a norm-convergent subsequence or a \(2\)-co-lacunary subsequence. This answers an open problem of Parcet and Randrianantoanina \cite[Remark~3.11]{ParcetRandrianantoanina2006} and removes both hyperfiniteness and semifiniteness.
item.dc:creator: Jinghao Huang, Yunpeng Zhu

item.title: Extensions of Operator Systems, Hyperrigidity and Quantum Double Suspension
item.description: arXiv:2610.18129v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a class of extensions of unital operator systems satisfying a certain Toeplitz type property. We show that these extensions induce corresponding extensions of the $C^*$-algebras they generate. We prove that hyperrigidity is preserved under these extensions, yielding new examples through iteration. We introduce the quantum double suspension of operator systems as a special class of these extensions and show that its iterates yield the Hong-Szyma\'nski quantum double suspensions at the $C^*$-algebra level, encompassing, in particular, the Vaksman-Soibelman quantum spheres. We construct hyperrigid operator systems underlying these quantum spheres. As a further application, we show that every counterexample to Arveson's hyperrigidity conjecture gives rise to a sequence of counterexamples. We identify the $C^*$-envelopes of these extensions and use this identification to obtain a $K$-theoretic condition ensuring that each such sequence contains infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic counterexamples. We also observe that the validity of the conjecture in the commutative setting is linked to its validity for an infinite family of noncommutative operator systems obtained through successive extensions. Finally, we compute the propagation number, an invariant of operator systems introduced by Connes and van Suijlekom, for these extensions.
item.dc:creator: Vibhor Bhatt, Satyajit Guin, Palash Sharma

item.title: Hereditary NC Polynomials & Positivity Domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.14053v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Noncommutative polynomials, elements of the free algebra generated by several noncommuting variables $x_1,...,x_g,x_1^*,...,x_g^*$, are of importance in noncommutative algebra, free analysis and real algebraic geometry. We allow matrix coefficients and view these noncommutative polynomials as functions in several size-free matrix variables. The free locus of a noncommutative polynomial $f$ is the sequence of hypersurfaces $\mathscr{Z}_n(f)=\{X\in M_n(\mathbb{C})^g:\det f(X) = 0\}$. When $f$ is Hermitian, the positivity domain of $f$ is the sequence of semialgebraic sets $\mathcal{D}_n(f)=\{X\in M_n(\mathbb{C})^g:f(X)\text{ is positive semidefinite}\}$. We show for well-behaved cases that the Euclidean boundary of the positivity domain is Zariski dense in the free locus. This leads to a certificate for equality of positivity domains of coefficient-irreducible unsignatured atomic quadratics. Finally, we describe the geometric structure of positivity domains of hereditary quadratic polynomials through $\Gamma$-convexity.
item.dc:creator: Abdellah Islam, Jurij Vol\v{c}i\v{c}, Hugo J. Woerdeman

item.title: Stabilizers and maximal subgroups of topological full groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.15253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study closed-set stabilizers in topological full groups of minimal effective ample groupoids with Cantor unit space. For almost finite or purely infinite groupoids, we extend the maximal stabilizer theorem of Grigorchuk and Vorobets to every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup. For a nonempty closed nowhere dense set, maximality of its stabilizer is equivalent to minimality of its stabilizer action, minimality of the regular reduction, and primeness of a canonical wide open subgroupoid. Without assuming almost finiteness or pure infiniteness, we prove spatial rigidity for stabilizers acting minimally on infinite closed nowhere dense sets. Their isomorphism types determine the ambient Kakutani equivalence class and, when Hausdorff, the effective reduction. We also realize every AF groupoid with compact unit space as the full restriction, with its relative topology, of any minimal effective ample groupoid with Cantor unit space to a closed nowhere dense subset. Combining rigidity and realization yields continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic stabilizers in every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup; these stabilizers are maximal when the ambient groupoid is almost finite or purely infinite. The realization also gives explicit AF subquotients of the ambient reduced groupoid $C^*$-algebra, including the CAR algebra, with compatibility on the canonical diagonal subalgebras.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Matui

item.title: Radial Schur multipliers on trees and the failure of Fourier-Schur transference
item.description: arXiv:2610.15881v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given $1 < p < \infty$ and a function $m \colon \mathbf{N}_0 \to \mathbf{C}$, we provide a characterization of radial Schur multipliers $M(x,y) = m(d(x,y))$ on the Schatten $p$-class of a tree $(X,d)$ equipped with its graph metric. That is, the operator norm of the radial Schur multiplier $S_M$ is controlled by the norm of the Fourier multiplier $T_m$ on the torus: \[ \big\| S_M \colon S_p(X) \to S_p(X) \big\|_{\mathrm{cb}} \lesssim \frac{p^4}{(p-1)^2} \, \big\| T_m \colon L_p(\mathbf{T}) \to L_p(\mathbf{T}) \big\|_{\mathrm{cb}}, \] with both quantities being comparable when the tree $X$ has infinite diameter. This is a rather unexpected inequality, which necessarily fails at the endpoints $p=1,\infty$ due to the work of Haagerup, Steenstrup and Szwarc. As an application, we construct the first examples of completely $S_p$-bounded Herz-Schur multipliers in the free group that are unbounded as Fourier multipliers. This result disproves Fourier-Schur transference---a longstanding open problem since the work of Neuwirth and Ricard in 2011. In line with this, our main result also implies the surprising fact that free balls Schur multipliers are uniformly $S_p$-bounded, in sharp contrast to their Fourier behavior. In addition, we disprove Fourier-Schur transference over the algebraic groups $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbf{Q}_q)$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbf{R})$ with $\mathrm{K}$-biinvariant counterexamples, the latter involving additional geometric and probabilistic techniques.
item.dc:creator: Adrian Gonz\'alez-P\'erez, Javier Parcet, Jorge P\'erez Garc\'ia, Simeng Wang

item.title: A higher categorical approach to graded bivariant $K$-theories for Real $C^*$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.17060v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present an $\infty$-categorical refinement of classical $KK$-theory and $E$-theory for graded, $G$-equivariant for a locally compact second countable group $G$, Real $C^*$-algebras. As a consequence, we obtain a couple of fiber sequences connecting the different $K$-theory spectra, and explicitly analyse the induced endomorphisms on $K_0$-groups. We also answer precisely some folklore questions in the area. Among other things, we show that graded $KK$- and $E$-categories are not a Dwyer-Kan localization of graded $C^*$-algebras.
item.dc:creator: Anupam Datta

item.title: Completely symmetric subspaces of noncommutative $L_p$-spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.18041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $2<p<\infty$. We prove that every infinite-dimensional closed subspace $F$ of a noncommutative $L_p$-space contains a subspace completely isomorphic to $\ell_p$, $C_p$, $R_p$, or $C_p\cap R_p$ and completely complemented in $F$. This answers the question of Junge and Xu on the existence of completely symmetric basic sequences.
item.dc:creator: Jinghao Huang

item.title: Algebraic Direct Sums and Generalized Drazin Invertibility
item.description: arXiv:2610.18433v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $T$ be a bounded linear operator on a complex Banach space $X$. We prove that the algebraic decomposition \[ X=\K(T)\oplus \Hq(T) \] forces both summands to be closed and hence characterizes generalized Drazin invertibility. This improves the classical characterizations of Mbekhta~\resultcite{Theorem~1.6}{MbekhtaKato}, Schmoeger~\resultcite{Theorem~4}{Schmoeger}, and Daji\'c and Koliha~\resultcite{Theorem~6.7}{DajicKoliha}, by removing their closedness assumptions. We also show that $T$ is generalized Drazin invertible if and only if \[ \dim\bigl(\K(T)\cap \Hq(T)\bigr)<\infty \quad\text{and}\quad \codim\bigl(\K(T)+\Hq(T)\bigr)<\infty. \] For ordinary Drazin invertibility, we obtain analogous finite-defect characterizations involving the hyperkernel and the hyperrange. We also give a characterization using pointwise nilpotence on an invariant summand. Finally, we consider arbitrary invariant algebraic decompositions and give a counterexample when the inverse of the restriction to one summand is not assumed bounded.
item.dc:creator: Zakariae Aznay, Fadil Chabbabi

item.title: Haagerup-Izumi modular data from hyperbolic words: S-fold TQFTs, central charge, torsion and the Bethe vacua
item.description: arXiv:2610.18512v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The modular data of the doubles of the Haagerup--Izumi categories is a grafting of two finite metric groups (conjectured by Evans--Gannon, proved for untwisted categories by Gannon--Schopieray--Yadav). Gang and Kim found non-unitary modular data of this shape in the topological twist of rank-$0$ $S$-fold theories, from the Bethe vacua of an abelianised gauge theory. The aim is to understand rigorously the significance of the handle-gluing and fibering operators, and to construct the Bethe vacua. For every hyperbolic once-punctured-torus monodromy $\varphi$, a word in $L$ and $R$, the two groups are $A_\mp=\coker(\varphi\mp1)$, with the torsion linking forms of the mapping tori of $\varphi$ and $-\varphi$. Over all words of trace $m^2+2$ these forms reproduce the Evans--Gannon table of Q-systems, one printed entry being corrected, and the distinct modular data in the list of Gannon--Schopieray--Yadav. The Bethe data are given in closed form by the word: the level matrix, the positive vacuum, $c_{\eff}=\#L$, and the handle-gluing values $2^{\#L}\lambda^{\pm1}|A_-||A_+|$ at the identity classes, $\lambda$ the stretch factor. Each kernel vector of $\varphi\mp1$ modulo $|A_\mp|$ at which an explicit trigonometric formula does not vanish gives a solution of the Bethe equations in closed form. Under the half-index dictionary, with the unit in the class of $\sigma V^*$, $c\equiv\#L-6\#R\pmod{24}$.
item.dc:creator: David E Evans

item.title: Simplicity of action-based $C^{*}$-algebras from hyperbolic actions
item.description: arXiv:2604.12520v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the simplicity of $C^{*}$-algebras built from group actions. For a faithful isometric action of a group $G$ on a countable metric space $X$, we use the associated action representation on $\ell^2(X)$ to define the action-based $C^{*}$-algebra $C^{*}_{X}G$. We define generalized versions of the properties $P_{\mathrm{naive}}$ and $P_{\mathrm{analytic}}$ relative to this action and show that the naive form implies the analytic form. We also prove that $P_{\mathrm{analytic}}$ associated with a coefficient-separating action representation ensures the simplicity of the action-based $C^*$-algebra. As an application, for every connected orientable boundaryless infinite type surface containing a connected nondisplaceable finite type subsurface, we deduce that its mapping class group satisfies the properties $P_{\mathrm{naive}}^{\mathbb{X}}$ and $P_{\mathrm{analytic}}^{\mathbb{X}}$ for one fixed hyperbolic space $\mathbb X$.
item.dc:creator: Tianyi Lou

item.title: Heisenberg-Weyl Representations and Morita equivalence for crossed products of Noncommutative solenoids
item.description: arXiv:2607.03353v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study strong Morita equivalence for crossed products of noncommutative solenoids by cyclic groups. Using their description as twisted group $\mathrm C^*$-algebras, we construct automorphisms induced by the natural linear action of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z[1/p])$ on $\mathbb Z[1/p]^2$, for every integer $p>1$. For odd primes, we use the Heisenberg--Weyl representation to construct compatible cyclic group actions on the equivalence bimodules relating solenoids with reciprocal parameters. This yields strong Morita equivalences between the corresponding crossed products by $\mathbb Z$ and, for finite-order matrices, by finite cyclic groups. The corresponding equivalence for flip crossed products for the action of $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ holds for every prime, including $2$. For prime $p$, we give representatives for the nontrivial finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z[1/p])$ and explicit arithmetic criteria for conjugacy among these representatives.
item.dc:creator: Pratik Kumar Kundu

item.title: $\mathrm{C}^*$-selflessness of groups of homeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2609.29399v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that $\mathrm{C}^*$-simple groups which admit a faithful extreme boundary are $\mathrm{C}^*$-selfless. More precisely, we establish complete selflessness of the canonical inclusion of the reduced group $\mathrm{C}^*$-algebra into the reduced crossed product. In particular, the Higman--Thompson groups and the Brin--Thompson groups are $\mathrm{C}^*$-selfless.
item.dc:creator: Ryoya Arimoto

item.title: $W^*$-categories are von Neumann
item.description: arXiv:2609.30015v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A $C^*$-category is to a $C^*$-algebra what a groupoid is to a group. An example is the category of Hilbert spaces and bounded linear maps, and indeed, every $C^*$-category can be represented as a sub-$*$-category of this. Analogously, a $W^*$-category is a $C^*$-category where every object has a predual, and we might expect a representation theory on Hilbert spaces where the resulting morphism spaces are $\sigma$-weakly closed. We identify a gap in the literature here, stemming from the (perhaps surprising) fact that a $C^*$-algebra can have a non-isometric predual and yet not be a $W^*$-algebra. Using the theory of dual TROs (ternary rings of operators) we repair this gap, and along the way, also give further justification to arguments in the literature about dual TROs. Motivated by the theory of Dual Banach Algebras, we offer an alternative axiomatisation of $W^*$-categories where we allow non-isometric preduals of the hom spaces, but require that they are additionally bimodules in a certain sense. This involves the theory of self-dual Hilbert $C^*$-modules.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Daws

item.title: Three-Point Trace Positivity:Schatten Norm Compression and Interpolating Metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.11021v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(\mathcal N,\nu)$ be a finite tracial von Neumann algebra and set $\mathcal{K}_r(P,Q)=\nu((P^{1/2}QP^{1/2})^r)$. We prove that $$ [\mathcal{K}_r(P_i,P_j)]_{i,j=1}^3\ge0, \qquad 1/2\le r\le1. $$ The range $1/2<r<1$ is new even for matrices, and order three is sharp for $1/2\le r<1$. This single mechanism resolves two problems. First, if $(\mathcal R,\omega)$ is finite tracial and $H=[H_{ij}]_{i,j=1}^3\in M_3(\mathcal R)_+$, then $$ [\omega(|H_{ij}|^p)]_{i,j=1}^3\ge0, \qquad 1\le p\le2, $$ settling the Lin--van den Driessche conjecture on Schatten norm compression. Second, for a semifinite tracial von Neumann algebra $(\mathcal M,\tau)$, define $$ d_t(A,B)^2=\frac{\tau(A)+\tau(B)}2- \|B^{t/4}A^{t/4}\|_{2/t}^{2/t}. $$ We prove that $d_t$ is a complete metric on $L^1(\mathcal M,\tau)_+$ for $1\le t\le2$, including the previously open range $1<t<2$ between the Hellinger and Bures endpoints, and that $$ d_t\text{ is a metric on }L^1(\mathcal M,\tau)_+ \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad t\in[1,2]\ \text{or}\ \mathcal M\text{ is abelian}. $$ Its topology and Cauchy sequences agree with those of $L^1$. The same classification holds for unital tracial $C^*$-algebras and, with the known $t=0$ obstruction, resolves Problem~2 of Kom\'alovics and Moln\'ar.
item.dc:creator: Trung Dung Vuong, Hiroyuki Osaka

item.title: Free probability via entropic optimal transport
item.description:
arXiv:2309.12196v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be compactly supported probability measures on $\mathbb{R}$, and let $\mu  oxplus 
u$ denote their additive free convolution. We show that for all sufficiently large real $z$,  egin{equation} \int_{-\infty}^\infty \log(z - x) \, (\mu  oxplus 
u)(\mathrm{d}x) = \sup_{\Pi} \left\{ \mathbf{E}_\Pi[\log(z - (X+Y))] - H(\Pi \mid \mu \otimes 
u) ight\}, \end{equation} where the supremum is taken over all couplings $\Pi$ of $\mu$ and $
u$. Analogous formulas hold for multiplicative free convolution $\mu  oxtimes 
u$ and free compression $[\mu]_	au$. In this way, integrals of a log-potential against free convolutions can be expressed as entropic optimal transport problems. The corresponding optimal couplings admit explicit formulas, from which the standard $R$- and $S$-transform descriptions of additive and multiplicative free convolution are recovered. In particular, the optimizer $\Pi_z$ encodes the subordination equations via couplings of random variables. Our approach is based on a large deviation principle on the symmetric group, combined with the quadrature method of Marcus--Spielman--Srivastava.
item.dc:creator: Octavio Arizmendi, Samuel G. G. Johnston

item.title: Extendable Shift Maps and the Canonical Map on Generalized Countable Markov Shifts
item.description: arXiv:2506.07487v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We obtain an operator-algebraic characterization of when the shift map can be continuously extended from a standard countable Markov shift $\Sigma_A$ to its generalized countable Markov shift $X_A$, a compactification of $\Sigma_A$. We show that a canonical unital completely positive map on the Exel--Laca algebra $O_A$ can be defined exactly when the shift extends continuously from $\Sigma_A$ to $X_A$, and that in this case its restriction to the maximal commutative C$^*$-subalgebra $D_A$ is a $*$-endomorphism to which the extended shift is dual. We also give a criterion on the matrix $A$ itself, in terms of the convergence of its columns, and exhibit classes of transition matrices satisfying these equivalent conditions. Column-finiteness of $A$ is necessary for the existence of the continuous extension. Finally, we construct an example in which the set of empty words is a Cantor set and the extended dynamics on it is the inverse of the dyadic odometer.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Bissacot, Iv\'an Diaz-Granados, Thiago Raszeja

item.title: Hilbert transforms on Coxeter groups and groups acting on buildings
item.description: arXiv:2508.18176v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we study Hilbert transforms and their boundedness on $L_p$-spaces associated with Coxeter groups and groups acting on buildings. We establish new models for Hilbert transforms on these groups through the geometric objects they act on, and we show that these Hilbert transforms satisfy a Cotlar identity which was developed in earlier work of Mei and Ricard, and that of Gonz\'alez-P\'erez, Parcet and the second named author, thus conclude the $L_p$-boundedness. We manage to solve the problem firstly for the case when the Coxeter group satisfies a certain nested condition, and then extend it to any finitely generated Coxeter groups and groups that admit actions on buildings satisfying the nested condition. Our results give the first example of groups with property (F$\mathbb{R}$) on which $L_p$-bounded Hilbert transforms can be defined, and generalize the work of Gonz\'alez-P\'erez, Parcet and the second named author for groups acting on simplicial trees.
item.dc:creator: Xiao-Qi Lu, Runlian Xia

item.title: A general proof of integer R\'enyi QNEC
item.description: arXiv:2605.15272v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the R\'{e}nyi quantum null energy condition for every integer R\'{e}nyi order $n\geq2$. In local Poincar\'e-invariant quantum field theory, this states that the sandwiched R\'{e}nyi divergence (SRD) of an excited state relative to the vacuum is convex along a future-directed null deformation. We assume that the deformation is realized by the canonical translations of a half-sided modular inclusion and that the divergence is finite for the initial, undeformed algebra. The proof establishes convexity of the SRD along the induced positive contraction semigroup on Haagerup $L^n(M)$, for every non-zero positive initial element. We also establish a R\'enyi ant formula at every even integer order and, under an additional regularity assumption, at odd integer orders. The R\'enyi ant formula identifies the negative first null derivative of SRD with a multiple of the infimum of the canonical null-translation energy over vector purifications of an escort state constructed from the excited state and the vacuum.
item.dc:creator: Tanay Kibe, Pratik Roy

item.title: Local Ocneanu rigidity for separable algebra objects
item.description: arXiv:2609.10440v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish local Ocneanu rigidity for separable algebra objects in Hom-finite monoidal categories C over an algebraically closed field k. A separability morphism contracts the first two Hochschild cohomology groups without requiring an abelian ambient category. Separable algebra structures and homomorphisms from separable sources have open algebraic-group orbits, and affine Bezout estimates give effective finiteness results. For Frobenius subalgebras, exchange relations replace the source and embedding data by a single self-dual idempotent. We prove that their separable inner-conjugacy classes are open in the exchange locus, yielding a bound of 2^(dim_k(End_C(X))) for any ambient Frobenius algebra X; connectedness gives the same bound on the actual number of subalgebras. As an application, we obtain an effective form of the Etingof-Walton finiteness theorem: every finite-dimensional semisimple Hopf algebra H over C has fewer than 2^(dim_C(H)) left coideal subalgebras. In the unitary setting, we bound E-compatible intermediates of C*-algebra and von Neumann algebra inclusions up to unitary conjugacy, under finite-index and finite-center hypotheses. For irreducible finite-index subfactors N < M, we improve the 9^[M:N] bound of Bakshi-Das-Liu-Ren to fewer than 2^[M:N] intermediate subfactors.
item.dc:creator: Tinhinane Amina Azzouz, Mainak Ghosh, Sebastien Palcoux
